stem.en: Two objects A and B have masses m and 4m respectively, and they have the same kinetic energy. If the speed of object A is v, what is the speed of object B, in terms of v? Give the multiplier only - so if the answer is 2v, enter 2.

explanation.en: Set the two kinetic energies equal: (1/2)mv² = (1/2)(4m)v_B². The masses and the halves cancel, leaving v² = 4v_B², so v = 2v_B and v_B = v/2. The heavier object must move at half the speed, not a quarter: a quarter of the speed would give one sixteenth of the energy, and halving the speed gives one quarter of the energy, which with four times the mass makes the energies match.

hints.en: Write down (1/2)mv² = (1/2)(4m)v_B² and cancel what is common to both sides. What is left is a relationship between v² and 4v_B².
Remember that speed is squared. Four times the mass needs the square of the speed to drop to a quarter, and the square root of one quarter is one half.
